title: The token check proves who signed it and who issued it, but never what it was for, so an anonymous token can be exchanged for admin scope
index_line: T-0086 · AUTH_DECISION · valid-but-mis-scoped token: signature+issuer verified, scope ignored → anonymous JWT escalated to admin · java · corroborated
invariant_violated: Token validation assumed that a correctly signed token from the right issuer is a token for the right purpose. The scope claim was never compared with the operation being authorised, so a token minted for the internal anonymous identity was accepted as authority to mint an admin-scoped token.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated POST to the token endpoint returns an internal anonymous-user JWT, even with anonymous access disabled
the attacker presents that JWT to the token-exchange/creation endpoint
the service verifies the signature and the issuer — both are genuinely valid, so the token is accepted
the token's intended scope is never compared against the scope of the requested operation
a new token is minted carrying admin authority while keeping the anonymous identity, so later requests appear as token:anonymous
the admin token creates a persistent admin account and deploys a plugin, giving code execution and a foothold that survives restarts

source.http.request.value: two unauthenticated API calls: obtain the anonymous JWT, then exchange it for a scoped token

guard.signature.value: the signature and issuer validation that passes correctly and is the only check performed

token.claims.value: the scope/audience claim that is present in the token and never enforced against the operation

sink.auth.jwt-verify.value: the token-verification/creation service whose acceptance decision is the whole vulnerability

preconditions.expr: the build is in the affected range
a token with a valid signature but the wrong scope is accepted for a privileged call

check.spec: curl -s -X POST http://HOST/access/api/v1/tokens -H 'Authorization: Bearer <low-priv-token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"scope":"applied-permissions/admin"}' | head -c 300

success: a token created with an anonymous identity carries admin authority and is accepted by admin endpoints
later audit entries show actor token:anonymous performing administrative actions
failure_like: the exchange endpoint rejects a token whose scope does not include token creation
the minted token keeps the anonymous scope and admin endpoints answer 403
false_positive: anonymous access being enabled by configuration is not this bug — the flaw is that a token is issued even when it is disabled, and that its scope is not enforced
a token that merely decodes to admin-looking JSON is not accepted until an admin endpoint acts on it

hazards: every JWT/OAuth deployment that checks signature and issuer and calls it done
token-exchange endpoints are scope amplifiers: they take a low-value token and mint a high-value one
the identity in the token can stay unprivileged while the scope becomes administrative, so identity-based detections miss it
non_transfers: issuers that bind audience/scope into the signature and verify it at every consumer
systems where a token exchange requires the subject to hold the requested scope

evidence.target: JFrog Artifactory self-hosted, access token service (CVE-2026-42016 with CVE-2026-42018 as the token source)

provenance.author: Wiz Research
provenance.corroborates: in-the-wild chain: CVE-2026-42018 returns an internal anonymous-user JWT to an unauthenticated POST /access/api/v1/aws/token/ even when anonymous access is disabled; CVE-2026-42016 lets that token be exchanged at POST /access/api/v1/tokens for an admin-scoped token because the service validates signature and issuer but not intended scope; admin token then creates persistent admin accounts and deploys Groovy plugins

provenance.author: JFrog (security advisories)
provenance.corroborates: vendor advisories: CVE-2026-42018 — Artifactory could return an internal anonymous-user token to an unauthenticated caller when anonymous access is disabled; CVE-2026-42016 — insufficient token validation allowing privilege escalation
